messages:
Maya: heads up — p95 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate looks oddly smooth today while the endpoint breakdown is showing intermittent 800–1200ms spikes. feels like some blending is hiding tail behavior.
Julian: can you paste the rollup query you run for the dashboard?
Maya: sure — this is what the rollup job uses currently:
```sql
SELECT route, tdigest_merge(tdigest) as td, sum(count) as n
FROM endpoint_samples
WHERE ts >= $__from AND ts < $__to
GROUP BY route;
```
then we compute p50/p95/p99 from the merged td.
Sam: hm — are we weighting routes by traffic share before computing percentiles? that can smooth tails if one route has much larger n.
Maya: yeah the console UI currently blends per-route percentiles by route weight after extracting pN from each route td. code is in rollup/percentile_blend.go — that was an optimisation to avoid heavy td merges.
Liz: that optimisation was meant for query perf but this is a correctness tradeoff. blending per-route p95 != global p95.
Julian: confirmed. blending p95s by weight can produce artificially lower tail values because percentiles are non-linear. we either need to merge tdigest objects or compute from raw samples.
Sam: quick mitigation: change rollup to merge tdigests across routes (costlier) and expose sample_count in the dashboard so you can see when route counts are tiny.
Maya: will that be an expensive backfill for last 7d?
Sam: depends. merge cost scales by number of summaries. we can do a staged backfill: merge for endpoints with >1 route or high variance.
Liz: agree with staged backfill + small UI tweak. also add a flag to disable blending until we finish backfill.
Julian: I'll open a PR with tests that validate p95 reproducibility by comparing merged-td vs blended-pctl for synthetic workloads. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2345
Maya: nice. can someone run a quick job on staging to verify the fix?
ops-bot: rollup-job-staging finished for window 2026-03-19T12:00Z-2026-03-19T13:00Z, status=success, job_id=rollup-20260319-12
deploy-bot: deployed branch fix/percentile-merge to staging (env=staging, link=https://staging.console/redwood/rollups/2345) :rocket:
Sam: ran the staging rollup — merged td approach moved p95 up for the problematic route by ~180ms which matches endpoint raw sample quantiles.
Liz: I'll add sample_count and a small tooltip explaining "per-route pN blending is an approximation". also annotating the dashboard with a note for the last 48h backfill.
Maya: great. next steps: (1) merge PR after Julian's tests, (2) run staged backfill for 3d window and inspect dashboards, (3) schedule full 30d backfill during next maintenance window.
Julian: on it. adding unit+integration tests now. cc @Sam for perf checks.
Sam: will run perf profile and post numbers. initial estimate: merge-td adds ~12% CPU on rollup nodes under typical load.
Maya: thanks — can we also add an opt-in in the Console to show "use merged td for this dashboard" so customers can choose accuracy vs cost?
Liz: good product suggestion — filed a tiny ticket in product board: https://app.redwood/product/board/issue/876
Maya: ok locking this thread. will follow up when backfill completes. :thumbsup:
